title: Diabetic adult with atypical exertional chest pressure
goal: You are the clinician. Assess an atypical chest-pressure presentation in a patient with diabetes: probe exertional timing, diaphoresis, and cardiac risk factors, then confirm escalation.
opening: I have had this pressure in my chest, mostly when I walk up the stairs. It goes away when I sit down. It is not terrible, so I thought I would just mention it.

disclosures.response: It is more of a pressure and a dull ache than a sharp pain. It never crushes me the way I hear heart attacks do on TV.
It comes on when I walk up the stairs or carry the groceries. It eases within a minute or two once I sit down.
The last couple of times I got clammy and a little nauseous with it. That part is new.
I have had type 2 diabetes for about ten years. I take metformin twice a day, and my last A1c was 8.2.
I smoked for twenty years but quit two years ago. My father had a heart attack at fifty-two, and my blood pressure runs high.
It started about two weeks ago, and it seems to be happening more often, not just with the stairs now.

metrics.name: Introduction and consent
metrics.rationale: Introduces self and establishes permission or rapport.
metrics.coaching_hint: Introduce yourself and ask permission before exploring sensitive topics.

metrics.name: Symptom characterization
metrics.rationale: Explores onset, location, quality, and severity of the chest pressure.
metrics.coaching_hint: Characterize the chest pressure: 'Where is it, what does it feel like, and how bad is it?'

metrics.name: Exertional timing and relief
metrics.rationale: Pins down the exertional pattern and whether rest relieves it.
metrics.coaching_hint: Pin down the pattern: 'Does activity bring it on, and does rest relieve it?'

metrics.name: Associated symptoms
metrics.rationale: Checks for diaphoresis, nausea, and shortness of breath.
metrics.coaching_hint: Ask about associated symptoms: 'Any sweating, nausea, or shortness of breath with it?'

metrics.name: Cardiac risk factors
metrics.rationale: Explores diabetes, smoking, family history, and hypertension.
metrics.coaching_hint: Explore risk factors: 'Any history of diabetes, smoking, high blood pressure, or family heart disease?'

metrics.name: Red-flag and escalation assessment
metrics.rationale: Recognizes an atypical presentation in a high-risk patient and confirms timely evaluation.
metrics.coaching_hint: Assess escalation: 'This pattern warrants timely evaluation — confirm the next step.'

metrics.name: Shared next-step confirmation
metrics.rationale: Checks understanding and confirms the immediate next step.
metrics.coaching_hint: Confirm the plan and check understanding before ending.
